html:
Wappynger is the map's spelling of the Wappinger, an Algonquian people of the east bank of the Hudson River, between Manhattan and the Poughkeepsie area, and into western Connecticut. They spoke a language close to that of the Munsee Lenape.

They farmed maize and fished, moving between river villages and inland hunting camps. Dutch traders of New Netherland reached them after 1609. In Kieft's War, from 1643 to 1645, the Dutch and the river peoples fought a bloody war that cost the Wappinger many lives. As settlers took their land, they sold most of it and moved away; many joined the Mohicans at Stockbridge, Massachusetts, in the 1700s. See Wappinger.
